body:
Stacked on #5976.

## What

This is the MessagePack counterpart of #5975. When an array opens and the input is contiguous, the reader reads the integers, floats, booleans and nils that follow in one tight loop (`parse_msgpack_scalar_run`). The loop switches on the head byte, loads the big-endian value straight from the input buffer and calls the SAX handler, instead of taking one trip through `parse_msgpack_internal` and `parse_msgpack_value` per element.

- Covered: positive and negative fixint, uint 8/16/32/64, int 8/16/32/64, float 32/64, nil, false and true.
- The loop stops at any other value and when fewer than 9 bytes are left. Those values go through the existing path, which reads them exactly as before.
- It runs once, when an array (fixarray, array 16, array 32) opens. As in #5975, a per-element check was not worth its cost.
- Non-contiguous inputs are unaffected (tag dispatch on the bulk-scan capability).

## Measurements

`from_msgpack` / `sax_parse` of the nativejson-benchmark files, B/A, with A = #5976. ab-harness one-binary A/B: GCC 13 instruction counts are from callgrind on x86-64; the Mac is an M1 Max with Apple clang (instructions retired, 60 reps).

| | GCC 13 instr | Mac instr |
|---|---|---|
| SAX canada | **0.639** | **0.485** |
| DOM read canada | 0.946 | 0.923 |
| SAX citm_catalog | 1.001 | 0.991 |
| DOM read citm_catalog | 1.004 | 1.000 |
| SAX twitter | 1.000 | 1.002 |
| DOM read twitter | 0.997 | 1.000 |
| strict UTF-8, citm_catalog | 1.003 | 1.001 |
| `std::istringstream`, citm_catalog | 1.003 | 1.002 |

No row is more than 0.4 % worse.

## Tests

New test case "MessagePack arrays of scalars from contiguous and non-contiguous input" in `unit-msgpack.cpp`. It reads a document with every head the loop handles, plus strings, bin and nested arrays inside and after the runs. It checks the values, then compares contiguous (`std::vector`) and non-contiguous (`std::list`) input for every truncation of the document:
- the `from_msgpack` result,
- the exception message,
- the full SAX event log,
- a SAX handler that stops after each of the first 60 events.

Planting a wrong value for negative fixints makes 100 assertions fail. The full ctest suite passes with ASan/UBSan.

## Breaking changes

None. Values, error messages, error positions and SAX events are unchanged. The public API is untouched.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

review_comments.body: In the CBOR version of this PR a few days ago, this "does it start with a scalar" function was dropped in favor of just calling the "read scalar run" so as to not duplicate checks.  Can the same thing be done here?  It looks like it would be a little more complex, and require that the do/while be converted to a simple while.  It might also require that there be `true_type` and `false_type` versions.
The next PR in the stack does exactly this "put the true_type/false_type test in the read scalar run function".

Right, done in `82e469a129`. `msgpack_scalar_follows()` is gone: `enter_msgpack_array` calls `parse_msgpack_array_start` directly, and `parse_msgpack_scalar_run` is now a `while` loop that checks the remaining count and length first. Its `default:` branch already leaves on anything that is not a scalar. Only `parse_msgpack_array_start` needed the `true_type`/`false_type` pair, and it already had one.

I measured both versions in one binary (instructions per repetition, new/old):

| case | clang (Mac) | GCC 13 (Linux, callgrind) |
|---|---|---|
| SAX twitter | 0.999 | 1.001 |
| SAX citm_catalog | 1.001 | 1.003 |
| SAX canada | 0.946 | 0.973 |
| read twitter | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| read citm_catalog | 1.000 | 1.001 |
| read canada | 0.991 | 0.992 |

So the pre-check did not pay for itself here: it repeated the three-range head test that the switch does anyway.

About the CBOR PR: you were right that it had been removed there, but 8bbfb5ec1d later put it back. I've removed it again in #5975 and replied in that thread with the CBOR numbers, so both readers are built the same way now.

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*
Is this function needed?  Can it be rolled into `parse_msgpack_scalar_run`?

Right, it isn't needed. The wrapper did two jobs: its tag kept non-contiguous inputs from instantiating the run, which uses `ia.bulk_data()`, and it was the function kept out of line. In `bc9912be25`, `parse_msgpack_scalar_run` takes the `std::true_type`/`std::false_type` tag and is `JSON_HEDLEY_NEVER_INLINE` itself, as `parse_ubjson_typed_run` already is on #5981, and `enter_msgpack_array` calls it directly. CBOR had the same wrapper, so `0ae85ec75f` on #5975 does the same there.

The run had a single caller, so little should change, and the counts agree: all within 1 %. Instructions per repetition, new/old, measured in one binary with Apple clang on an M1 Max:

| case | MessagePack | CBOR |
|---|---|---|
| SAX twitter | 0.999 | 1.000 |
| SAX citm_catalog | 1.001 | 1.001 |
| SAX canada | 1.007 | 0.995 |
| read twitter | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| read citm_catalog | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| read canada | 0.999 | 0.999 |

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*
Does this `back()` get elided when `bulk_scan` is false, or should it be pushed into `parse_msgpack_scalar_run`?

Right, it's cleaner inside. `back()` has no side effect in an optimized build, so the compiler should drop it, but it is still a call at `-O0`, and a hardened standard library keeps its non-empty check. In `3385afd86e` the run takes only the tag: the bulk version reads `container_stack.back().remaining` itself, the way the old wrapper did, and the `false_type` version takes nothing. `b1b6a1535e` does the same for CBOR on #5975. Instructions per repetition, new/old, on the Mac with Apple clang, are within 1 % on every row (0.993 to 1.001).

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

title: MessagePack reader: read runs of scalar array elements in one loop
